title: Council Rejects Adding Marcos Aranda as Early Voting Site for Dec. 12 Mayoral Runoff
excerpt: At a special meeting on Nov. 13, District 8 Councilwoman Alyssa Cigarroa asked the Laredo City Council to add Marcos Aranda Recreation Center as an early voting location for the Dec. 12 mayoral runoff. The council rejected the motion.
content:
The Laredo City Council rejected a proposal to add Marcos Aranda Recreation Center as an early voting location for the Dec. 12 mayoral runoff during a special meeting on Thursday, Nov. 13.

District 8 Councilwoman Alyssa Cigarroa, who is also a candidate for mayor in the runoff, asked that the center be added to the list of early voting sites. She said residents west of Interstate 35 were being underserved and that the center had drawn strong voter turnout in past elections. She described the current voting arrangement as an attempt to suppress the vote.

City staff explained that District 8 already had a designated early voting location at the Webb County Elections Office, which must remain open as the main voting site. Staff said District 5 received a second early voting location, at Joe Guerra Library, because of heavy voter turnout there. No specific turnout figures for Marcos Aranda Recreation Center were presented during the discussion.

Cigarroa led the field in the Nov. 3 mayoral election, and incumbent Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño finished second. The two face off in the Dec. 12 runoff, a citywide race in which any eligible Laredo voter may cast a ballot at any early voting location.

After the discussion, the council rejected the motion to add Marcos Aranda Recreation Center to the runoff early voting locations.

Update — Nov. 18, 2026: The dispute is still unresolved. At a City Hall debate on Monday, Nov. 16, council members were in the process of making a motion to add Marcos Aranda Recreation Center as an early voting site, but the meeting ended at 11 p.m. when a state-mandated deadline forced it to adjourn, before a vote could be taken. Councilwoman Melissa Cigarroa said closing a site in a district where it draws the highest vote totals is “fundamentally unfair and undemocratic.” Councilwoman Alyssa Cigarroa said the only other option on the west side of Interstate 35, the Webb County Elections Office, is frequently blocked by passing trains. City officials said they could not make changes, saying the Secretary of State was blocking modifications because early voting is set to begin Monday, Nov. 23. Cigarroa also said the arrangement would confuse District 8 voters, who would have to vote in one location for one election and travel across town for another.

Source: Video of the City Council Special Meeting, Nov. 13, 2026.
